purpose: V8.2.2 object-level access for the railway module. RailwayController checked only the caller's role (@Roles); no handler or service method checked that the wagon, GU-12 request or demurrage record belongs to the caller's organisation. Measured on the pre-fix service: a LOGISTICIAN of org-attacker set an org-logistics-001 wagon to MAINTENANCE, put it into its own GU-12, submitted another organisation's GU-12, calculated and stored demurrage for a foreign and for a non-existent wagon, and GET /railway/gu12 and GET /railway/demurrage returned every organisation's records; GET /railway/wagons?orgId= returned any organisation's fleet. Found as a P2 note by the independent session review of #5044 and widened by measurement here.
requiredInvariants: The check lives in RailwayService, not only in the controller, so no other caller can skip it. Every method that reads or mutates a wagon, GU-12 request or demurrage record takes the actor.

The privileged role set (ADMIN, SUPPORT_MANAGER, EXECUTIVE) comes from the existing ObjectAccessService.isPrivileged, not a second list. Its assertSameOrg is deliberately not used because it passes an object whose ownerOrgId is empty; here an empty organisation on either side is a refusal.
Not found stays 404 and is decided before access; access is 403 (RAILWAY_CROSS_ORG_ACCESS_DENIED). A refused mutation leaves the object unchanged and a refused create stores nothing.

No web caller of /railway exists (searched apps/web), so the tightened responses break no screen. No schema, migration, dependency or production change. V8.2.2 is not claimed: it is FAIL for the RLS reasons its note records, and railway is not cited there.

Existing tests in railway-body-validation.spec.ts keep every assertion; only their calls pass the owner actor, and the global wagon count is observed through a privileged view (3 for the owner plus 1 for the other organisation instead of 4 from an unscoped list).
acceptance: apps/api jest src/modules/railway: 2 suites, 41 tests pass (27 existing + 14 new).
Mutations, each caught: making the organisation check a no-op fails 7 of the 14 new tests; dropping the GU-12 list filter fails 1.
